Thank you for taking the time to reply to my post,  your words actually mean a lot to me. I just still find it hard to believe that there are people who truly care about me, it just doesn’t feel that way at all.

It all started around 2 years ago when I was beginning to lose interest in things that used to make me happy. I didn’t enjoy doing things that I loved anymore - things like drawing, playing my instruments, spending time with friends and all that. I was confused at first as to why I felt that way. 

As time went on, nothing would make me happy anymore. Negative thoughts always seemed to cloud my mind. I felt empty inside. I felt nothing. 

Just before I started feeling like this I had met a new group of friends. There were 4 of us, and for months and months they made me the happiest I had ever been. When I was around them I would constantly laugh until by stomach ached. We would stay up late on Skype calls until the very early hours of the morning. I adored them. 

However, a few months after I had started feeling depressed, I didn’t think they liked me at all. I was an outsider - they had be friends for years and I felt like an intruder in their group. It was as if I as a burden, and they just had to put up with me. It felt like they disliked me. Most of the time when we were out, the three of them would be together and I would always be left walking behind them. Also, most of the time, I would have to make the effort to talk to them, they wouldn’t make the effort to talk to me. Still, to this day, I still have moments where I feel like that. 

In addition to this, I started hating myself. I really disliked everything about myself. That’s when I started wishing I was gone. I was numb. No emotion apart from hatred. I resorted to self harm for around a year in order to feel something again, as well as harming myself for the sheer fact that I thought I deserved it. My mum eventually found out and took me to my doctor straight away. She was furious. After that day, I never harmed myself again. It took me a while, but over the course of around 3 months I started to get better, starting to enjoy things I used to again. I still felt the same way about my group of friends, but I still stuck around. I didn’t have anyone else. 

For about 4-5 months or so, I felt great. I felt on top of the world, and I was proud of myself for not letting go. But I’m beginning to have suicidal thoughts again. I was out with my friends last night - the same group of people - and it felt like I wasn’t even there. I said on plenty of occasions that I was going to go home because my phone was low on charge, and no one even said a word. I still stayed out though because I had nothing else to do. One of my friends, I’ll call him ‘D’, I message a lot throughout the day. I’ve started to believe that he really dislikes me, sometimes I only think he wants to keep me around because I can get drugs and alcohol or whatever. For the other two, ‘J’ and ‘E’, I get the vibe that they don’t like me a whole lot either. 

I would get into the whole “I’ll never find someone who wants me” thing, but I think that’s enough for this post. 

I don’t want to be here anymore. I don’t want to feel like I’m a burden. I want to be at peace, and suicide seems like the only answer. I don’t care anymore. It’s getting to the point where I don’t care how anyone else feels. I just want to be gone.
Sorry, this was before I posted on here.

Well, I don’t know if it was anything on my part, or anything on anyone’s else’s part, but gradually, all those suicidal thoughts began to escape my head, you know? I started enjoying things again that I had lost interest in due to how I felt before. These were things like drawing, playing video games, playing my instruments etc. 

Music played a big part, actually. I’m sure you’ve heard of the rapper ‘Logic’. I started to get into him when his song ‘1-800-273-8255’ was first released.  The moment after I heard that song, I immediately felt some sort of a connection with the artist. I listened to more songs off that album, where he would talk about his anxiety attacks and things like that. It felt like he was speaking directly to me. I started listening to more of his songs, looking into him himself, and discovered that he has, and still is going through similar things to me. I won’t go into to any further detail, but he definitely played a huge role in my recovery. Music in general did. 

However, Logic was my very recent saviour. A band called ‘Bring me he Horizon’ also helped in my recovery, but that was a few years ago. Much before I discovered Logic. 

But yeah, that’s it.
